## D-218 - does the heating move, and does it move deeper? (2026-09-10)

**What prompted it.** D-217's iteration 7, read against iteration 6:

     it   group        cells   entry Te   photoionization heating per H
      6   cold -> hot   8336      88 K       4.47e-23
      7   started hot   5293    4052 K       2.53e-25   (these are 6's flippers)
      7   cold -> hot   2835     701 K       1.13e-21

The cells that went hot at iteration 6 lose their photoionization heating by a
factor 180 and cool to 416 K; a different set of cells takes 25x more than
iteration 6's group did. The heating is not a property of fixed cells.

**The hypothesis.** Heating per H nucleus goes as x(H0) times the field above
threshold. Cells that ionize at iteration N carry few absorbers at N+1: the
hard photons pass through them to the layer behind, which heats, while the
ionized layer - little H0 to absorb with - loses its heating, cools, recombines
and becomes opaque again. An ionization front advancing in pulses. It predicts
that each iteration's cold -> hot cells are (a) deeper than the previous
iteration's, and (b) drawn from the previous iteration's stayed-cold cells.

**The history this has to respect.** Deep-cell heating is 99.5% H I
photoionization (D-138). The field delivering it is 86-100% stellar with no
packet crossing tau > 20 (D-159), which retracted the "photons that cannot
arrive" framing: the heating is real and the opacity that stops it belongs to
the other ionization state. D-168 raised a transport defect again and retracted
it at D-169. D-160 tested for a stable neutral branch under pdrTeFromMocassin
and found none. So this entry does not re-open the transport question; it asks
how the ionized/neutral alternation propagates through the grid.

**A claim from the running commentary, withdrawn.** While reading D-217 I
suggested a two-iteration delay between molecule formation and the opacity the
photons see, and that a delayed loop explains the 4-5 iteration period. The
structure does not support it. `iteration_mod` zeroes `grid%opacity` and runs
`ionizationDriver` - and so `addOpacity` with `H2den` - over every cell at the
TOP of each MC iteration, before the transfer. Photons at iteration N see H2
from iteration N-1's chemistry and an x(H0) normalised with `elemAvail` from one
iteration earlier still, because `updateCell` precedes the chemistry (D-216).
That lag errs OPAQUE while molecules form - more H2 arrives before x(H0) falls -
so it opens no transparent window where the collapse begins. It is recorded,
not used.

Also checked on the way: H2 opacity does reach the transport (the PDR build
passes `grid%H2den` to `addOpacity`, continuum above 15.43 eV), and
`pdrSplitField` is diagnostic-only - every `Jdif` read in `update_mod` sits
behind `lgDebug`.

**The instrument.** Per D-217 outcome group, on pass 1:

    A_V (mean)                     - depth
    x(H0), f_mol                   - the absorbers
    J above hydrogen's threshold   - sum of Jste from HlevNuP(1), the bin the
                                     H0 cross section itself starts from (ph_mod)
    tau per cell at threshold      - opacity(HlevNuP(1)) x cell size
    group one iteration ago        - none / cold->hot / stayed cold / started hot

The last needs the same cell across iterations, so `grid%budGrpLast` stores
each cell's group. Ownership of a cell is fixed per rank, so each rank carries
its own cells' history with no reduction. It is allocated in `setMotherGrid`
AND `resetGrid` - D-217 found the warm path missing every per-cell PDR array
added since D-188, and this does not add another.

**Run.** `runs/d218-front`, one-pass fixture, launched automatically as soon as
`runs/d217-budget` released the cores.

**What is NOT known.** Whether the flipping cells are deeper and were cold the
iteration before. If they are not - if the heating lands in scattered cells
with no progression in A_V - the pulsing-front picture is wrong, and patchy
Monte Carlo sampling of a hard-tail field deep in the cloud becomes the
leading alternative.



### D-218 result so far - iterations 4 to 6 (2026-09-10)

`runs/d218-front`, one-pass fixture. The trajectory reproduces `d217-budget`:
iteration 6's cold -> hot group is 8265 cells entering at 87.6 K with
photoionization heating 4.48e-23 per H, against 8336 cells, 88 K and 4.47e-23
in the earlier run.

**Checks.** At iteration 4 every cell's previous group is "none", as it must be.
Cells re-enter the census consistently: iteration 4's 587 started-hot cells cool
to 99 K and appear at iteration 5 as stayed cold (585 of them). Cells with no
previous group at later iterations are cells that joined the PDR zone between
iterations. tau per cell at threshold in the cold groups at iteration 4-5 is
1260-1270, matching D-168's independent 1270.

**The opacity trails the ionization by one iteration plus the damping.** With
n_H = 100, sigma(13.6 eV) ~ 6.3e-18 cm^2 and 2e18 cm cells, tau = 1260 per cell
is x(H0) = 1.0 exactly. At iteration 5 the cold groups report tau 1262-1270
while their x(H0) is 0.05-0.21. The census's end-of-iteration x(H0) median -
the state `ionizationDriver` reads at the top of the next iteration - is 0.998
after iteration 4 (seed defect: `elemAvail` never republished), 0.365 after
iteration 5 (0.21 from `updateCell` blended by iterDamp 0.25 with 0.998), and
0.110 after iteration 6. That predicted tau ~ 460 per cell for iteration 6's
photons; the flipping group measured 466. Confirmed.

**The cells that flip are not a front's leading edge.**

     it 6          cells   A_V    f_mol   tau/cell@thr   J>thr      phot heat   cold at it 5
     cold -> hot    8265   2.34   0.904      466        2.84e-3    4.48e-23       8262
     stayed cold    6579   2.10   0.680      598        1.77e-4    1.00e-24       6415

A front advancing outward would put the flipping cells shallower than the rest,
next to the previous iteration's hot cells. Instead they are the deepest and
MOST MOLECULAR cells, drawn almost entirely from the previous iteration's cold
cells - so their H0 opacity for this iteration's photons has fallen the
furthest (tau 466 against 598), and they receive 16x the field above threshold
and carry 45x the photoionization heating. Iteration 5's 33 flippers show the
same shape: deepest (A_V 2.54 against 2.25), f_mol 0.914, all cold the iteration
before, 47x the field.

What that suggests, and it is NOT yet a mechanism: molecular locking removes H0,
and H2 does not replace it as an absorber between 13.6 and 15.4 eV, so the
cells that lock most hydrogen lose the most opacity in that window - one
iteration late, because the opacity is built from the previous ionization.
The difficulty it has not resolved: tau ~ 466 per cell at threshold is still
far too thick for threshold photons to cross several cells, so the extra field
must sit at energies where the gas is thinner, and which band that is has not
been measured.

**Two slips while reading this.**
  - An awk field offset printed the PHOTOELECTRIC column as "photoionization
    heating" for iteration 6 (1.89e-25 for the flippers). Caught before being
    reported as a result; the values above are from the parser.
  - D-218's x(H0) is read from `grid%ionDen` after `updateCell`, so for cells
    that went hot it is the HOT END STATE, not what they carried into the
    solve. Pairing it with entry heating - x(H0)*J predicts only a ~1.4x
    heating ratio against the measured 45x - is not valid. f_mol is valid
    (`updateCell` does not move H2), and so are the field and tau columns,
    which do not depend on the solve.

**What is NOT known.** Which band carries the extra field - the 13.6-15.4 eV
window where H2 is transparent, or above 15.4 eV where it absorbs - and what
share of the photoionization heating is hydrogen's in these cells at ENTRY.
Those decide whether the missing absorber is H2 line opacity MOCASSIN does not
model, or something else.

### Iteration 7 reverses it (2026-09-10)

     it 7          cells   A_V    f_mol   tau/cell@thr   J>thr      phot heat   last iteration
     cold -> hot    2835   1.73   0.417      591        1.14e-2    1.17e-21    560 c->h, 2275 cold
     stayed cold    6890   2.50   0.518      248        2.12e-4    7.91e-25    2486 c->h, 4304 cold
     started hot    5256   2.11   0.219      167        1.52e-6    2.61e-25    5219 c->h

Every feature of the iteration 5-6 flipping group is inverted. The cells that
flip at iteration 7 are the SHALLOWEST, the LEAST molecular, and see the HIGHEST
tau per cell at threshold - and they receive 54x the field of the cells that
stay cold and 7500x that of iteration 6's flippers. Iteration 6's flippers, now
the started-hot group, see the LOWEST threshold tau (167) and receive the least
field of any group.

**Withdrawn.** The index row committed with iterations 4-6 read "the cells that
flip are the most molecular, and their H0 opacity has fallen furthest", and the
body offered molecular locking removing H0 absorbers as what it suggested. That
held at two iterations and is contradicted at the third. Tau per cell at H0
threshold does not predict where the field lands: at iteration 6 lower tau went
with more field, at iteration 7 higher tau does. Group means across three
iterations were read as a law.

**What survives iteration 7.**
  - The opacity trails the ionization by one iteration plus damping - measured
    at iterations 5 and 6 against a prediction, and the largest group at
    iteration 7 (started hot, tau 167) is consistent in magnitude with the
    end-of-iteration-6 median x(H0) of 0.110 (tau ~ 139).
  - The heating moves between cells every iteration (D-217), and cells rarely
    stay in one group: of iteration 7's stayed-cold cells, 2486 flipped at
    iteration 6.
  - Threshold tau being irrelevant to where the field lands is itself
    informative: the photons carrying the heating must sit at energies where
    the gas is far thinner than at 13.6 eV. That band is still unmeasured, and
    after iteration 7 it is the measurement that matters rather than one of
    several.

and 11 the lowest-tau group (started hot: 167, 130) receives the least field of

damping: tau 1260 at iteration 5 is x(H0) = 1.0 exactly, matching the

**What is NOT known.** Why the field in a cell collapses the iteration after the
cell heats, and which energy band carries the field that does arrive. The first
is a question about how the MC estimator responds to a cell's own state; the
second is the measurement proposed alongside the D-219 fix.

## D-219 - the opacity's hydrogen does not add up (2026-09-10)

Found while checking the first D-218 block. Its stayed-cold group reported
x(H0) = 0.9988 and f_mol = 0.5208 at iteration 4 - a hydrogen budget of 1.52,
where `x(HI) + 2x(H2) + x(HII) = 1` is the sharpest test in the project.

**Iteration 4 first, because it is a defect in D-209.** `seedMolecules` calls
only `seedAbunFromMocassin`. `pdrToMocassin`, the only writer of `elemAvail`,
runs inside the coupling loop (iteration_mod:1652) and after the D-200 damping
(1944) - both after iteration 4's `updateCell` (1115). So at the first PDR
iteration the ionization is normalised to the full hydrogen abundance while the
seed has already made half of it molecular.

**But the budget fails at every iteration, not only the first.** The census
line `[D196] x(H0)+2x(H2)+x(H+)`, across four runs:

     it   d210-budget        d215-cooltab       d216-restructure   d217-budget     
          median (min-max)   median (min-max)   median (min-max)   median (min-max)
      4   1.210 (0.98-1.73)   1.852 (1.00-1.99)   1.850 (1.00-1.99)   1.851 (1.00-1.99)
      5   1.050 (0.32-1.41)   1.260 (0.52-1.73)   1.263 (0.52-1.73)   1.261 (0.52-1.73)
      6   1.012 (0.18-1.43)   0.426 (0.34-1.51)   0.456 (0.34-1.49)   0.425 (0.34-1.59)
      7   1.003 (0.42-1.58)   1.329 (0.29-1.72)   1.364 (0.29-1.62)   1.343 (0.29-1.72)
      8   1.001 (0.27-1.70)   1.225 (0.28-1.73)   1.225 (0.28-1.72)   1.225 (0.28-1.73)
      9   1.000 (0.17-1.72)   1.088 (0.28-1.74)   1.090 (0.28-1.72)   1.088 (0.28-1.74)
     10   1.000 (0.14-1.71)   0.657 (0.28-1.72)   0.687 (0.27-1.73)   0.646 (0.27-1.72)
     11   1.000 (0.13-1.72)   1.067 (0.28-1.70)   1.063 (0.28-1.72)   1.071 (0.28-1.72)
     12   1.000 (0.23-1.56)   1.217 (0.27-1.72)   1.218 (0.27-1.68)   1.217 (0.27-1.72)

**It is the state the opacity is built from.** The census takes x(H0) and x(H+)
from `grid%ionDen` and 2x(H2) from `grid%pdrAbun` (iteration_mod:2099-2102) and
prints at line 2196 - after the D-200 damping (1905) and the `elemAvail`
republish (1944). At the top of the next MC iteration `ionizationDriver` reads
`grid%ionDen` as-is - `density = ionDenUsed * elemAbun * Hden`, no
renormalisation - and hands `addOpacity` `grid%H2den`, which follows `pdrAbun`
(D-201). So this table is the hydrogen the photons of the next iteration see.

**Why it happens.** The ionization is solved once and the chemistry then moves
the molecular content. The ionization carries x(H0) normalised to the
molecular fraction BEFORE that move; the molecules carry the fraction AFTER.
When H2 forms, hydrogen is counted twice (median 1.85, 1.26, 1.36); when H2 is
destroyed, it is missing (0.43 after iteration 6's collapse, 0.66-0.69 after
iteration 10's).

**It is not new with D-216, but D-216 made it permanent.** The pre-D-216
one-pass run (`d215-cooltab`) gives the same series. The five-pass run
(`d210-budget`) holds the median at 1.003, 1.0007 ... 1.0000 from iteration 7,
because its last `updateCell` uses `elemAvail` from chemistry that had
converged over the passes. D-216 moved `updateCell` out of the loop to stop the
temperature march, and in doing so reinstated - at the scale of a whole MC
iteration - the lag D-199 had removed at the scale of a pass. D-216 was
committed without checking this budget. It is the test CLAUDE.md singles out,
and it should have been run before calling D-216 done.

Even at five passes individual cells span 0.13-1.72, so the median closing is
not the same as every cell closing.

**What it does and does not explain.**

  - RETRACTED: "It is NOT the collapse trigger. Iteration 6 enters with a
    median of 1.26 - an excess, which errs opaque." The budget sum counts H2,
    and H2 has no continuum between 13.6 and 15.4 eV (D-139); at hydrogen's
    threshold the only gas absorber is H0. The H0 fraction iteration 6's
    photons saw had fallen to 0.365 of atomic from 1.0 one iteration earlier
    (measured under D-218). So the lag errs TRANSPARENT at threshold exactly
    when molecules form. What still stands is that `d210-budget`, with its
    median at 1.00, also collapsed - so the lag is not NECESSARY for a
    collapse. Whether it triggers this one is open.
  - It plausibly AMPLIFIES what follows a collapse. After iteration 6 the median
    cell's opacity carries 0.43 of its hydrogen, and iteration 7 then carries
    the largest photoionization heating in the run, 1.13e-21 per H in its
    flipping cells (D-217). After iteration 10 it carries 0.65, and iteration
    11's heating is elevated but less so (1.02e-22). Two cases in the same
    direction, which is a correlation and not a mechanism.

**What is NOT known.** Whether the cells that flip are the deficit cells - a
per-cell question the group means cannot answer. And whether `updateCell` is
itself consistent with the `elemAvail` it is handed at the start of an
iteration: D-218's per-group x(H0) + f_mol at pass 1 measures exactly that, and
decides where a fix must act.

**The fix is not applied.** The candidate is D-153's rule applied on MOCASSIN's
side: after the chemistry moves the molecular content, rescale the linked ion
stages to the new `elemAvail` - MOCASSIN keeps the RATIO between stages, the
chemistry sets the non-molecular TOTAL - before the opacity is built. Plus a
`pdrToMocassin` after `seedMolecules`. It changes the D-216 design, so it is
put to the operator rather than made.


---

## D-220 - the ion stages brought to the same hydrogen as the molecules (2026-09-10)

**What.** A new `rescaleIonToAvail`, called in `iteration_mod` after the D-200
damping block closes - so after the last change to the molecular content and
the last `elemAvail` republish, whether or not the damping ran. For every
enabled element, stages `1..min(elem+1, nstages)` are scaled so they sum to
`min(max(elemAvail, 1e-10), 1)`. That is exactly the normalisation
`ionBalance`'s conservation row imposes (`availFrac`), so this applies the next
`updateCell`'s normalisation one step earlier, where `ionizationDriver` needs it
to build the opacity. The ratio between stages is MOCASSIN's and is unchanged;
the total is the chemistry's. D-153 hands the chemistry MOCASSIN's ratio and
keeps the chemistry's total; this is the same split applied on MOCASSIN's side.

Elements `pdrToMocassin` never sets keep `elemAvail = 1` and are unchanged.
At the call site `ionDen` is already reduced and every rank has republished
`elemAvail` from the reduced `pdrAbun`, so every rank rescales identically and
no collective is added.

Also a `pdrToMocassin` immediately after `seedMolecules` at `pdrStartIter`: the
seed moves the molecular content and nothing republished `elemAvail`, so the
first PDR iteration's `updateCell` normalised hydrogen's stages to 1 beside a
seed that had made half of it molecular (budget 1.85 at iteration 4, D-219).

**Verification built in.** The D-196 budget census prints after the rescale, so
its median should read ~1.00 rather than 0.43-1.85 - the other hydrogen carriers
in the network (H2O, OH, CH_n, H3+) keep it slightly off. And a `[D220]` line on
rank 0 reports hydrogen's mean |x(H0)+x(H+)+2x(H2)-1| and the fraction of cells
off by more than 1% BEFORE each rescale, so the defect is measured in the same
pass that removes it.

**What it is not.** A promised cure. `d210-budget`, whose median budget was
1.000 from iteration 7, still collapsed at iterations 6 and 11. The fix makes
the opacity physically consistent; whether that changes the collapse is what
the run measures.

---

## D-221 - which band carries the heating (2026-09-10)

**Why.** D-218: threshold opacity does not predict where the field lands - at
iterations 7 and 11 the lowest-tau group receives the least field - so the
photons carrying the heating must sit where the gas is much thinner than at
13.6 eV. The candidates differ in what they imply: in the 13.6-15.4 eV window H2
has no continuum (D-139; MOCASSIN does not model H2 line opacity there), above
15.43 eV H2 absorbs (`addOpacity` with `yanH2xSec`).

**What.** At the D-217 entry call (the first `thermBalance` of the updateCell),
H0's photoionization heating is split inside the frequency loop at the first
bin with nu >= 1.1345 Ryd, with exactly the scaling `heatIonSte` gets, and
stored in per-cell `mocBand(cell, 1:2)` - allocated in `setMotherGrid` and
`resetGrid`. The census adds per outcome group: the field summed over
[HlevNuP(1), split) and [split, nbins], the two H0 heating means, and H0's share
of the group's entry photoionization heating.

**Run.** `runs/d220-fix`, one-pass fixture, carrying both D-220 and D-221.

**What is NOT known.** Everything the run is for.


### D-220/D-221 verified at runtime - iteration 4 (2026-09-10)

`runs/d220-fix`, one-pass fixture.

**The rescale works as designed.** At the end of iteration 4:

    [D220] rescaled ion stages to elemAvail in 15204 cells;
           before: mean |x(H0)+x(H+)+2x(H2)-1| 0.4004, off by >1% in 14186 (93.30%)
    census budget after the rescale: min 0.99996  median 1.0000  max 1.0000

Before the rescale the defect is large and nearly universal - the chemistry
moved the mean molecular fraction from the seed's 0.52 to 0.78 during the
iteration, and 93% of cells carried an ionization normalised to the old value.
After it the budget closes exactly. That the maximum departure is 4e-5 also
bounds the network's other hydrogen carriers (H2O, OH, CH_n, H3+) below that
here, so the ~1.25% D-196 once attributed to them was lag, as D-199 concluded.

**The seed republish works.** At pass 1 of iteration 4, x(H0) + f_mol per group
is 0.992, 0.999 and 0.981 (the last before x(H+)) - against 1.41 and 1.52 at
the same point in `runs/d218-front`, where `elemAvail` was never republished
after the seed. tau per cell at threshold is still 1260 at iteration 4, as it
must be: iteration 4's opacity was built before the seed ran. The first opacity
built from the rescaled state is iteration 5's, and should read ~272 per cell
from the end-of-iteration-4 elemAvail(H) of 0.2160.

**D-221 is internally consistent.** The two bands reproduce D-218's total field
above threshold to four figures in every group (6.707e-9 + 2.463e-7 = 2.530e-7
against 2.531e-7; 2.820e-8 against 2.820e-8; 2.198e-6 against 2.198e-6). H0's
share of the photoionization heating is 0.9950, 0.9404 and 0.9913 - never above
1, and matching D-138's 99.5% and D-168's 99.7% independently.

**A first look at the band - eight cells, not a result.** Iteration 4's eight
cold -> hot cells receive 97% of their field above 15.43 eV, and 99.97% of their
H0 heating comes from that band (1.135e-25 against 2.9e-29 in the window). The
13,980 cells that stay cold receive 89% of their field in the 13.6-15.4 eV
window. If iteration 6's thousands of flipping cells show the same, the heating
that flips cells comes from photons H2 does absorb, and missing H2 line opacity
in the window is not the cause.

First iteration whose transfer was built from the rescaled state.

     cold -> hot     10    2.52   0.906     121       0.000       3.93e-4       0.000        4.78e-24       0.984

**Prediction met.** From the end-of-iteration-4 elemAvail(H) of 0.2160 the
bulk of the cold gas should see tau ~ 0.216 x 1260 = 272 per cell at threshold;
the 14,700 stayed-cold cells measure 281. `runs/d218-front` read 1262-1270 at
this iteration. The rescale reaches the opacity, which is the path D-219 said
was broken.

**The band shifted, and not in the way the window hypothesis would predict.**
In the stayed-cold cells the field above 15.43 eV rose from 3.0e-9 at
iteration 4 to 2.28e-6 at iteration 5 - a factor ~760 - while the window field
stayed near 3e-8. At iteration 4 the window carried 89% of their field; at 5
the hard band carries 98%. Lowering the H0 opacity at threshold 4.5-fold did
not bring in window photons; it coincided with the hard band arriving.

**Flipping cells, two iterations running.** Iteration 5's ten flippers receive
exactly zero field in the window and take all their H0 heating from above
15.43 eV, as iteration 4's eight did (99.97%). Eighteen cells in total, so
still not a result - iteration 6 is where thousands flip.

**What is NOT known.** What absorbs the hard band on the way in - H0, H2 above
its 15.43 eV threshold, He above 24.6 eV, or dust - and so why lowering the H0
fraction moved it by ~760x. That is a question for a per-absorber opacity
decomposition, and is only worth building if iteration 6 shows the same.

**The band, at scale.**

     it 6          cells   A_V   f_mol  tau@thr   J 13.6-15.4   J >15.4   % hard   H0 heat win   H0 heat >15.4   H0 share
     cold -> hot    7274   2.28  0.902    124     6.61e-9       3.30e-3    100.0    3.20e-29      4.94e-23        0.993

The 7274 cells that flip receive 99.9998% of their field above 15.43 eV and
take essentially all their H0 photoionization heating from that band - six
orders of magnitude more than from the window. H0 is 99.3% of their
photoionization heating. 7270 of them were cold the iteration before. The cells
that stay cold are also hard-field dominated (99.96%); only the 64 shallow
started-hot cells, at A_V 0.65, are window-dominated.

**So the window hypothesis is ruled out.** The heating that flips cells is not
carried by 13.6-15.4 eV photons slipping through gas where H2 has no continuum.
It is carried by photons above 15.43 eV - the band where H2 does absorb, and
where the flipping cells, at f_mol 0.90 and n(H2) ~ 45 cm^-3, should be very
thick near threshold (tau ~ 900 per cell at 18 eV from yanH2xSec).

**What that leaves.** The photons arriving must sit where every absorber is thin
- well above threshold, where the H0 and H2 cross sections fall as E^-3 and
E^-3.5 and He0 has not yet taken over (24.6 eV) or has fallen off again. Which
energies those are, and which absorber sets the path on the way in, is not
measured. The obvious next instrument is the hard band split further in energy,
with the opacity along it decomposed by absorber (H0, H2, He, dust). It is not
built.

**Also noted.** Convergence at iteration 6 is 0.1118% (17 cells), against
0.0132% without the fix. Both are tiny and this is one run of each, so no
weight is put on it.

## D-222 - what the hard photons cross (2026-09-10)

**Why.** D-221: the heating that flips cells arrives above 15.43 eV, at every
iteration from 4 to 12, with hydrogen doing 99.5-99.9% of the absorbing. The
cells it lands in are about 90% molecular - n(H2) ~ 45 cm^-3 - and yanH2xSec puts
H2 at ~1e-17 cm^2 near 18 eV, so tau ~ 900 per cell there. For photons in that
band to reach them the gas must be thin at their energy, and neither the energy
nor what sets the path is measured.

**The bands.** Edged at physical thresholds rather than chosen numbers:

    1  13.6  - 15.43 eV   HlevNuP(1) to the H2 continuum threshold (the D-221 window)
    2  15.43 - 24.59 eV   H2 continuum to He0 (HeIlevNuP(1))
    3  24.59 - 54.42 eV   He0 to He+ (HeIIlevNuP(1))
    4  54.42 - mid        He+ to the geometric middle of [He+ edge, top of grid]
    5  mid   - top

In this fixture the top of the grid is nuMax = 15 Ryd = 204 eV, so the split
sits near 105 eV. Each band's representative bin is the one at its geometric
centre. `setHardBands` in `common_mod` finds all of them once, from nuArray and
the H0/He0/He+ pointers, and the heating loop, `addOpacity` and the census all
read the same edges.

**What is recorded.**

  - Per band, per outcome group: the field (sum of Jste over the band) and H0's
    photoionization heating at the entry call. The heating is accumulated inside
    `thermBalance`'s frequency loop with exactly the scaling `heatIonSte` gets,
    in `mocBand(cell, 3:7)`; D-221's two values stay in (cell, 1:2).

  - At the representative bin of each hard band (2-5): tau per cell of each gas
    absorber - H2, free-free, H0, He0, He+, heavier elements - plus dust
    (absOpac + scaOpac), plus the total opacity the transport used.

**How the absorber split is taken.** Not by recomputing cross sections in the
census: by the time the census runs, `updateCell` has already moved `ionDen`, so
a recomputation would describe a different state from the one the photons saw -
the pitfall D-218's x(H0) column fell into. Instead `addOpacity` snapshots the
running opacity total at the four bins after each stage it already performs in a
fixed order (H2, free-free, H0, He0, He+, heavier elements), and each absorber's
share is the difference between successive snapshots. That is the opacity as
built, by construction.

`ionizationDriver` runs on a rank chosen by an iCell counter that carries across
grids, while the census's counter resets per grid - they agree for this
single-grid fixture and would not in a multi-grid model. So the capture,
`grid%opaRep(cell, 4, 6)`, is zeroed with the opacity at the top of each MC
iteration and summed across ranks exactly as the opacity is, rather than relying
on the two ownerships lining up.

**The check built in.** The transport's tau is dS x `grid%opacity` and its
scattering probability is scaOpac/opacity, so `grid%opacity` is the total with
dust included. The census prints (gas components + dust) / total at each
representative bin; it should read 1.

Allocated in `setMotherGrid` and `resetGrid`.

**Run.** `runs/d222-absorbers`, one-pass fixture, carrying D-220 (so the budget
is closed) and D-221.

**What is NOT known.** Everything the run is for.


### Iteration 4: the instrument checks out (2026-09-10)

`runs/d222-absorbers`, first D-222 block.

**The split is complete.** (gas + dust) / total reads 1.0000 at all four
representative energies in all three groups: the captured absorbers plus dust
reproduce exactly the opacity the transport used.

**The bands reproduce D-221.** Cold -> hot: window field 4.54e-9 against D-221's
4.542e-9; the hard bands 9.51e-8 + 3.83e-8 + 0 + 0 against D-221's 1.334e-7 above
15.43 eV. H0 heating 2.32e-26 + 1.00e-26 against 3.321e-26. Stayed cold
1.37e-9 + 1.75e-9 against 3.116e-9; started hot 1.57e-7 + 1.04e-7 against
2.607e-7.

**H2's opacity is exactly zero at all four energies in every group - expected
at this iteration, required to change at the next.** Iteration 4's opacity was
built at the top of the iteration, before `seedMolecules` placed any H2. From
iteration 5 on H2den is populated when the opacity is built, and H2 must
appear; if it does not, H2 is not reaching `addOpacity` and the measurement
cannot answer its question.

**What iteration 4 shows, from five flipping cells.**

### Iteration 5: H2 reaches the transport, and no energy lets photons cross these cells (2026-09-10)

**H2 is in the opacity from iteration 5, as required.** At 19.8 eV H2's tau per
cell is 690 in the cold -> hot cells and 611 in the stayed-cold bulk, where
iteration 4 read exactly zero. (gas + dust) / total is still 1.0000 at every
bin in every group.

     it 5, cold -> hot (7 cells)   H2     H0     He0    He+    Z      dust   total
     tau/cell @  19.8 eV           690    57      -      -     1.2    0.40   ~750
     tau/cell @  36.9 eV           115    9.7    74      -     0.83   0.29   ~200
     tau/cell @  75.4 eV           10.6   1.15   16.1   0.011  0.29   0.25   ~28
     tau/cell @ 149.5 eV           1.29   0.14   2.59   0.002  0.07   0.21   ~4.3

The field is again zero above 54.4 eV in every group, and the flipping cells
take all their field (1.10e-4) and all their H0 heating (2.75e-24) from
15.4-24.6 eV.

**A narrow-window hypothesis, tested and refuted.** The representative bin
samples a band at one energy, and `yanH2xSec` is negative at its threshold and
clamped to zero (the code says so) before rising to its peak near 18 eV - so a
transparent sliver just above 15.43 eV, where molecule formation has also
removed the H0, was possible and invisible to one bin at 19.8 eV. Evaluating
`yanH2xSec` exactly as coded, with a hydrogenic H0 cross section, and the
cells' own H2 and H0 columns inferred from their measured tau at 19.8 eV:

  - The clamped region is real: sigma_H2 is exactly 0 from 15.43 to ~15.7 eV,
    1.5e-18 at 15.8 eV, 9.8e-18 at 18 eV.
  - But H0 keeps it thick. Minimum tau per cell over 15.4-25 eV is 116, at
    15.61 eV, in the flipping cells (n(H2)dx 8.8e19, n(H0)dx 2.8e19 cm^-2) and
    206 in the stayed-cold bulk. Tau per cell is below 100 nowhere in that range.
  - At 36.9 eV the measured total is ~200; above 54.4 eV there is no field.

The inferred columns carry the hydrogenic approximation, but a minimum of 116 is
some 50 e-folds from transparent, so a factor of a few does not change it.
**There is no energy at which photons present in the field can cross one of
these cells.**

**What that implies, and what it does not.** The field recorded inside the
flipping cells did not travel through them. It must be deposited in a skin a
fraction of a cell deep - entering from a neighbouring cell's face - or be
emitted locally. MOCASSIN's J is the path length accumulated over the cell's
whole volume, so energy absorbed in a thin skin is spread over the entire cell
and heats it uniformly.

**Hypothesis - not tested.** The relaxation oscillation is substantially a
resolution artefact. These cells are 2e18 cm on a side at tau 100-1000; a real
ionization front is of order 1/(n sigma) ~ 1e15-1e16 cm, a hundredth to a
thousandth of a cell. A cell whose illuminated skin should ionize while its
interior stays molecular instead has the skin's heating spread over its whole
volume; with a bistable thermal balance the whole cell flips rather than
partially warming. Once flipped it is ionized, carries few absorbers and loses
~1000x of its field (D-218's second regularity), and the next cell inward
receives the flux in its skin and flips in turn - a front advancing about one
cell per iteration regardless of the physical front speed. It is consistent
with every result that survived the physics fixes: the collapse is unmoved by
the seed (D-209), the cooling extrapolation (D-215), the chemistry loop
(D-216) and the hydrogen budget (D-220); the heating moves between cells every
iteration (D-217); flipping cells come from last iteration's cold cells and lose
their field the iteration after (D-218); and it is carried by photons the gas
cannot transmit (here).

**What would test it.**
  1. Adjacency, cell by cell: whether each iteration's cold -> hot cells are
     face-neighbours of cells that were hot or flipped the iteration before.
     A front artefact predicts nearly all are; scattered heating predicts few.
     The group means cannot answer this.
  2. Whether the field in the flipping cells is stellar or diffuse
     (`pdrSplitField`, diagnostic-only per D-218's check).
  3. Resolution: the oscillation's amplitude, period and front speed at a
     finer grid. Most expensive; 58^3 is the memory ceiling at nbins = 600.

The second collapse reproduces `runs/d220-fix`: iteration 10 median f_mol 0.305
against 0.315, Te median 787 K against 762 K.

**The clamped H2 sliver, per iteration.** Near 15.6 eV only H0 absorbs; from each
iteration's flipping-cell H0 column that tau per cell is ~2.04 x the H0 value at
19.8 eV: 88, 380, 290, 143, 78, 110, 312 at iterations 6-12. The minimum, 78 at
iteration 10, is still some 34 e-folds from transparent.

**The sharpest observation in the table.** The flipping and stayed-cold cells
see almost the same opacity - 747 against 703 per cell at iteration 10, 758
against 698 at iteration 6 - but the flipping cells receive 16-32x the field. It
is not how thin the gas is that picks the cells that flip. It is how much field
reaches them, in a band neither group can transmit.

**Conclusion of D-222.** No energy present in the field lets photons cross one
of these cells, at any iteration. The field recorded inside the flipping cells
did not travel through them; it entered a skin from a neighbouring cell or was
emitted locally, and MOCASSIN's volume-averaged J spreads it over the whole
cell. D-223 distinguishes the two.

## D-223 - neighbours, and the diffuse share (2026-09-10)

**What.** Two additions to the D-217 census, per outcome group, on pass 1.

  - **Adjacency.** For each cell, its six face-neighbours; a neighbour counts as
    hot if its iteration-start Te exceeds 3000 K. Reported: the percentage of
    cells with at least one hot neighbour, the mean number, and the percentage
    with at least one hot neighbour upstream (lower A_V) and downstream. The
    stayed-cold group is the control: if flipping cells border hot cells no more
    often than stayed-cold cells do, adjacency is not what selects them.

    The neighbour's state is its `TeIterStart`, which every rank holds for every
    cell because it is copied from the reduced grid. `budGrpLast` would have been
    the natural "flipped last iteration" flag, but it is only valid on the rank
    that owns a cell, and a neighbour is often owned by another rank. Upstream is
    decided by A_V rather than by distance from the star, so nothing is assumed
    about where the source sits in the symmetric grid.

  - **Diffuse fraction.** With `pdrSplitField` set, `Jdif` holds the diffuse
    packets alone while `Jste` holds both. Reported: Jdif/Jste summed over the
    window, 15.4-24.6 eV and 24.6-54.4 eV (above 54.4 eV there is no field).
    A skin fed by stellar photons arriving from the source side predicts a low
    diffuse fraction; local or neighbour emission predicts a high one.

**`pdrSplitField` is diagnostic-only, now checked in `iteration_mod` too.**
D-218 found every `Jdif` read in `update_mod` behind `lgDebug`. In
`iteration_mod` the switch only zeroes `Jdif` each iteration (line 577), sums
it across ranks (790), applies the same 1e-9 unit scaling (856) and the same
octant division (870) as `Jste`. Nothing there uses it for physics. A new
fixture, `benchmarks/pdr/hiipdr-split`, is `hiipdr-couple1` with
`pdrSplitField 1` and nothing else.

**Run.** `runs/d223-adjacency`, built on all four flavours and launched
automatically once `runs/d222-absorbers` released the cores.

**What is NOT known.** Everything the run is for.


### Result (2026-09-10)

`runs/d223-adjacency`, 12 iterations, 23:19, clean exit. The collapse reproduces
`runs/d222-absorbers` (median f_mol 0.239 at iteration 6 and 0.300 at 10,
against 0.239 and 0.305), confirming empirically that `pdrSplitField` changes no
result. Every diffuse fraction lies in [0, 1] and the upstream/downstream counts
never exceed the at-least-one count.

**Adjacency, by iteration-start Te > 3000 K:**

           cells  >=1 hot  up     cells  >=1 hot  up        cells  >=1 hot
      6     7345   0.03%   0.01%   7506   1.52%   1.49%        68   98.5%
      7     3177   41.9    28.6    7016   43.7    37.5       4787   96.7

At the collapse the flipping cells are not next to hot cells at all - fewer of
them than of the control, and with only 68 hot PDR cells at iteration start
there was nothing for a front to advance from. The count includes non-PDR
neighbours, so the H II region's edge would have registered. At every later
iteration the flipping cells border hot cells at the control's rate, upstream
and downstream alike. Adjacency to a hot cell does not select the cells that
flip.

**Diffuse fraction.** Jdif/Jste is 0.05-0.12 in every group and band at every
iteration - at iteration 6, 0.112 / 0.070 / 0.075 in the flipping cells against
0.076 / 0.072 / 0.066 in the control. The field is ~93% stellar everywhere,
flipping cells included. Local or neighbour emission does not put it there.

**So both routes D-222 left open are closed**, and the resolution-artefact
hypothesis recorded there - a front advancing one cell per iteration from hot
neighbours - is refuted as stated.

**What the transport is not doing.**
  - **No thick-cell crossing.** Zero `[D159]` lines in twelve iterations: no
    stellar packet on rank 0 crossed a cell with tau > 20 without interacting.
  - **No importance weights.** `calculate_pass_prob_and_weight` keeps only the
    analog draw, passProb = -log(1-random) with weightFactor = 1; every biased
    scheme in it is commented out. New packets start at weight 1.0.
  - **No forced skip.** The exp(-tau) branch D-146 found was removed at D-147.
  - **No carried-over field.** `Jste` is zeroed before every transfer
    (iteration_mod:575) and nothing blends it across iterations.
  - **No fresh optical-depth budget mid-path.** `absTau` is reset in exactly
    two places, each paired with a new passProb: at the start of a path
    (photon_mod:1262, drawn at 1274) and after an interaction that re-launches
    the packet (1861, drawn at 1870).

**D-146's open question is back.** D-146 measured the field decaying as
tau ~ 0.9 per cell against a stored 250-450 and recorded it Open; D-147 removed
the forced skip, which explained the exact zeros but, as D-146 said itself, not
the shallow attenuation. D-159 rebutted the framing on the grounds that the
failing cells were nearly transparent - x(H0) = 0.026 giving tau ~ 6 per cell at
1.79 Ryd, computed from H0 alone. That rebuttal does not reach the D-222 cells:
their opacity was captured from `addOpacity` itself, includes H2, reproduces the
transport's total exactly, and is at least ~80 per cell at every energy carrying
field. Stellar packets are nevertheless being absorbed in them, at 16-32x the
rate of neighbours with the same opacity, without any recorded crossing of a
thick cell.

**What the Te criterion cannot see.** The photons care about a neighbour's
optical depth, not its temperature. A neighbour that is transparent in band 2
but below 3000 K - a cell still ionized while it cools under iterDamp, for
instance - is invisible to this census and is exactly the kind of channel that
would let stellar packets reach a flipping cell's face. The next adjacency test
should use the neighbour's tau per cell at the band's representative energy.
Failing that, a packet-level trace - for band-2 stellar packets absorbed in PDR
cells, the cells crossed and the optical depth accumulated - is the direct
measurement.

## D-224 - neighbours by optical depth, and the transport trace (2026-09-11)

**Why.** D-223 closed both routes D-222 left open - no hot neighbour, no local
emission - and left two things standing: the flipping cells take 16-32x the
control's 15.4-24.6 eV stellar field at the same ~700-760 tau per cell, and
D-146's measured attenuation (~0.9 per cell against a stored 250-450) was never
explained. A packet absorbed in an opaque cell deposits a path of ~1/kappa, so
an opaque cell's J measures the energy *entering* it. 16-32x the field at the
same opacity is 16-32x the energy entering. Either it crosses a face from a
neighbour the photons can cross - which a Te test cannot see - or the transport
charges some steps to a cell they are not in. Both are measured in one build.

**1. Adjacency by optical depth** (census, pass 1, per outcome group). For each
cell, among its six face-neighbours (in the PDR zone or not), the one with the
smallest tau per cell at band 2's representative bin (19.8 eV), from
`grid%opacity` - the array the transport used this iteration, reduced across
ranks. Reported: the histogram of that minimum (<0.1, 0.1-1, 1-10, 10-100,
>=100), its mean log10; for that neighbour, whether it is in the PDR zone, its
iteration-start Te and x(H0), whether it is upstream in A_V; and the share of
cells with any upstream neighbour below 1 per cell.
  - Flippers with a transparent neighbour, control without: the channel is
    physical, and the question becomes why that neighbour is transparent at the
    temperature it has.
  - Neither group with one: the field in the flippers did not come through a
    face, and part 2 should show how it got there.

**2. Transport trace** (photon_mod, every packet, every iteration). Where
`tauCell = dS*opacity(xP,yP,zP)` is formed, the step's start point and length
are checked against the box of cell (xP,yP,zP): walls midway between axis
points and the axis ends at the grid edges - the same walls the wall distances
are measured to - with a tolerance of 1e-3 of a cell width (single-precision
position resolution at 6e19 cm is ~4e12 cm, ~2e-6 of a cell). Counted:
  - steps starting outside their cell;
  - steps longer than the chord to the cell's far wall, and the excess path;
  - how often the "cater for cells on cell wall" branch replaces a wall
    distance. Read from the code, when a packet sits exactly on a wall the
    j-loop advances the index and that branch then sets the distance to
    `xAxis(nx)`, the grid's extent, without computing the distance to the next
    wall of the new cell. A step taken after it could run through several cells
    while charging one cell's opacity and J. Whether it fires in this geometry
    is not known from reading.

For 15.4-24.6 eV stellar packets - the band that carries the heating that flips
cells (D-221, D-222) - also: every interaction in a cell with tau per cell > 20
is binned by the tau per cell of the cell crossed immediately before ("none"
when the path began in that cell, at launch or after a dust scattering), and
flagged if the previous step or this one was not inside its cell, if the
interaction point is outside the cell, and if the previous cell is in the PDR
zone. Per cell, the band's path-length estimator is split into the part
deposited by steps not inside their cell and the part deposited by steps
entering from a cell below 1 per cell; the census reports both shares per group.

**Diagnostic only.** Behind `pdrSplitField`, as D-159's probe is. The counters
are summed and printed, never read by the physics, and no random number is
drawn, so the packet histories are those of D-223. The fixture is `hiipdr-split`
unchanged; the run should reproduce `runs/d223-adjacency` to Monte Carlo
scatter.

**What is NOT known.** Everything the run is for.

`runs/d224-trace`, fixture `hiipdr-split`, 14 ranks. Iterations 1-7 read here;
the run continues to 12.

**Adjacency by optical depth.** At iterations 4, 5 and 6, in every outcome
group, 100% of cells have their most transparent face-neighbour above 100 per
cell at 19.8 eV; none has any upstream neighbour below 1 per cell; the share of
the band's stellar field from steps entering from below 1 per cell is 0.

**What it means.** The PDR zone is sealed at 19.8 eV: every cell in it,
including the ones on the H II edge, has only neighbours above 100 per cell -
the ionization front itself sits in the non-PDR cells, which are where the
opaque-cell interactions happen (their previous cells are never PDR cells). The
cells on the H II edge hold 3.3e-7. The flipping cells, walled in by PDR cells
at ~700 per cell, hold 3.2e-3 - four orders more - and ~93% of it is stellar
(D-223). For a stellar packet to interact in a flipping cell its previous cell
would be a PDR cell, and that count is zero at every iteration.

**Refuted here.**
  - A transparent-but-cold neighbour channel (D-223's open point): there is no
    neighbour below 100 per cell.
  - Steps charged to a cell they are not in, including via the wall-snap
    branch: 2-7e-7 of steps, none in the band.
  - Packets crossing opaque PDR cells in sequence: previous cell >= 100 per cell
    in 0-0.1% of opaque interactions, and never a PDR cell.
  - The opacity being rebuilt between the transfer and the census, so that the
    census reads a different opacity than the photons saw: `grid%opacity` is
    written only at the top of the MC iteration (zeroed, `ionizationDriver`,
    reduction, dust), before `energyPacketDriver`; `addOpacity` is called only
    from `ionizationDriver`, which is called only there.
  - A NaN in the outputs: the single match was the label `nAngleBins`. No NaN
    or negative-opacity warning in the log.

**Caveats.** "Previous cell in the PDR zone" reads `pdrZone` inside the
transport on every rank; that it is valid there is inferred from its reduction,
not checked. The census shares are shares, not absolute values, so they cannot
say whether the traced stellar estimator in the flipping cells is small or zero.
Both are removed in D-225.

## D-225 - closure: is the field deposited by transport at all? (2026-09-11)

**Why.** D-224 leaves the flipping cells' 15.4-24.6 eV field unexplained by any
transport event it traced. Every write to `Jste` in the source was listed: the
two deposits in `pathSegment` (crossing and interaction), the same pair in
fluorescence_mod (fluorescence is off here), the zeroing, the copy back from the
reduction (a straight copy by `active` index) and the uniform 1e-9 and 1/8
scaling. So either the field there is deposited by steps the trace classified
without its being visible in shares, or something that is not in that list
writes into `Jste` - an out-of-bounds write into adjacent memory is the obvious
candidate, and would be invisible to every census so far.

**What.** `trcJ` grows to six columns:
  4. the path-length estimator for every packet in the band, stellar or
     diffuse, added in both branches exactly as `Jste` is;
  5. stellar interactions in the cell;
  6. stellar steps in the cell.

**Checkpoint 1** (right after the transfer, reduction and scaling): over all
cells, the sum of `Jste` over 15.4-24.6 eV and the scaled sum of column 4, their
ratio, and the number of cells differing by more than 1e-3.

**Checkpoint 2** (census, per outcome group): per cell, `Jste` and the traced
total, their ratio and the share of cells not closing; `Jste - Jdif` against the
traced stellar estimator; stellar interactions per cell and stellar steps per
cell, counted where they happen rather than inferred from the previous cell's
zone.

Closure at both: the flippers' field is deposited by transport steps in those
cells, and the step counts say which. Closure at 1, not at 2: something between
the transfer and the census writes `Jste`. No closure at 1: something inside the
transfer writes `Jste` outside the deposits - next is a bounds-checked build.

**Run.** `runs/d225-closure`, fixture `hiipdr-split` with `maxIterateMC` cut to
7 in the run's copy of the input (iteration 6 is the collapse; nothing before it
depends on the iteration cap). Diagnostic only, behind `pdrSplitField`.

**What is NOT known.** Everything the run is for.

the field is entirely diffuse, which is what D-223 printed (0.05-0.12) and what

~93% stellar in every group" and "local or neighbour emission does not put it
there". The copy back now also runs under `pdrSplitField`; nothing reads Jdif for
physics unless `lgDebug` (D-218), so no result changes.

The checks that should have caught it: a diffuse fraction that sat near 1/14 in
every group at every iteration, and a Jdif never compared against a total.

## D-226 - the re-emission spectrum of cold cells (2026-09-11)

**Why.** D-225: the 15.4-24.6 eV field that heats the flipping cells is diffuse.
A diffuse packet's frequency is drawn from the `recPDF` of the cell it is born in
(photon_mod, newPhotonPacket), after the line/continuum choice by `totalLines`.
`recPDF` is built by emission_mod (`fb_ff`, `twoPhoton`, `setDiffusePDF`) at the
top of each MC iteration from that cell's Te, Ne and ion fractions, then reduced.
It is a normalized shape: however little a cold cell emits in total, the PDF
decides where the energy it absorbs is re-emitted. A photon re-emitted in the
band inside a cell at ~700 per cell is absorbed on the spot, re-emitted from the
same PDF, and deposits ~1/kappa each time.

**What reading the code found.**
  - H I bound-free (analytic branch) starts at the threshold bin `HIPnuP`, with
    exp(-(nu - nu_th)h/kTe): at 260 K nothing above 15.4 eV.
  - Heavy-element edges carry the same decaying factor above their edges.
  - He I 2^3S (19.82 eV, the `j2TsP` bin): proportional to Ne x(He+), rate taken
    at max(5000 K, Te).
  - **The He I and He II analytic branches start at the top edge of their
    tabulated range, `HeINuEdgeP(nlimGammaHeI)` and `HeIINuEdgeP(nlimGammaHeII)`,
    not at their thresholds.** The tables end at 1.7999 Ryd (He I threshold
    1.8072 Ryd) and 3.9996 Ryd (He II, 4.0). If the start rounds to a lower bin
    than the threshold, that bin - the top bin of 15.4-24.6 eV for He I - gets
    exp(+(nu_th - nu)h/kTe), which grows as Te falls, with a cross-section index
    that lands before the He I block, in the free-free array (~3e-22 cm^2 there,
    against 7.4e-18 at threshold). The factor for a 0.0073 Ryd gap is ~40 at
    315 K, ~8e4 at 102 K and ~3e10 at 48 K; times the cross-section ratio
    (~4e-5), negligible at 300 K, comparable to the threshold emission at 100 K,
    dominant below. The collapses follow the coldest iterations - median Te
    102 K at the end of iteration 5 and 133 K at the end of 9 (D-224).

That is an inference from code and three numbers, and it depends on whether
1.7999 and 1.8072 Ryd fall in different bins of this frequency grid, which
reading cannot settle. It is the leading candidate, not a finding.

**What.**
  - One-time report from `fb_ff` (rank 0): for H I, He I and He II, the bin the
    analytic branch starts at, the threshold bin, their frequencies, and the
    cross-section read at the start and at the threshold.
  - Census, per group: the probability that a re-emitted packet is born in
    15.4-24.6 eV, (1 - totalLines) x the recPDF increment summed over the band;
    the bin carrying most of it and its share; the field's top bin and the field
    share in the top-probability bin; x(He+), x(H+), the line fraction, and the
    share of cells whose iteration-start Te is below 100 K.
  - A top bin at ~24.5 eV that holds the field is the He I branch; at 19.8 eV the
    2^3S term; elsewhere a heavy-element edge (Ar I 15.76, Fe II 16.2, Si II 16.35,
    Ne I 21.56, S II 23.3, C II 24.38 eV).

**Run.** `runs/d226-emission`, fixture `hiipdr-split` capped at 6 iterations.
Diagnostic only.

**What is NOT known.** Everything the run is for.


### Result (2026-09-11)

`runs/d226-emission`, fixture `hiipdr-split` capped at 6 iterations, 14 ranks.
Closure (D-225 checkpoint 1) holds at every iteration; the collapse reproduces
(7237 flipping cells at iteration 6 against 7322 in D-225).

**Edge report** (`fb_ff`, rank 0, once):

     continuum   analytic start bin (nu, Ryd)   threshold bin (nu, Ryd)   xSec read at start   xSec at threshold
     H I          430 (0.99943)                  430 (0.99943)             -                    -
     He I         465 (1.79220)                  467 (1.80797)             3.372e-22            7.431e-18
     He II        516 (3.99970)                  517 (4.00000)             2.240e-23            1.587e-18

The He I branch starts **two** bins below threshold, not one, and bin 465 is
0.0158 Ryd below it. Its factor relative to the threshold emission, with the
cross-section ratio (4.5e-5), is ~0.1 at 315 K, ~2e6 at 102 K and ~1e18 at 48 K.
He II's gap is 3e-4 Ryd and there is no He++ here, so it contributes nothing in
this model - but it is the same defect.

**Census: probability that a re-emitted packet is born in 15.4-24.6 eV**

     it  group         cells   P(band)    top bin (share of P)   field in that bin   Te_start<100 K   x(He+)    x(H+)
      4  cold -> hot       4   2.78e-3    19.78 eV (0.815)       0.232 (top: 23.11)    0%            2.2e-2    4.0e-3
      4  stayed cold   13975   2.62e-4    19.78 eV (0.846)       0.882                 0%            6.4e-4    9.2e-4
      4  started hot     569   6.51e-3    19.78 eV (0.763)       0.773                 0%            1.2e-3    1.9e-2
      5  cold -> hot      13   0.954      24.38 eV (1.000)       1.000                23%            1.5e-4    3.6e-2
      5  stayed cold   14702   0.0848     24.38 eV (0.999)       1.000                 0.16%         4.8e-4    1.3e-3
      5  started hot      74   3.87e-3    19.78 eV (0.848)       0.867                 0%            2.1e-3    4.7e-2
      6  cold -> hot    7237   0.983      24.38 eV (1.000)       1.000                85%            1.7e-5    7.1e-2
      6  stayed cold    7617   0.349      24.38 eV (1.000)       1.000                14%            1.9e-4    8.6e-3
      6  started hot      64   2.93e-3    19.78 eV (0.850)       0.891                 0%            2.6e-3    5.7e-2

**What it means.** The mechanism of the relaxation oscillation, end to end:
  1. A PDR cell cools (iteration-start Te of a few hundred K and below).
  2. Its re-emission spectrum collapses into bin 465: at 24.38 eV, just below
     He I's threshold, the analytic branch's exp(+(nu_th - nu)h/kTe) outgrows
     every real term, however little He+ there is - the flipping cells hold the
     least (1.7e-5).
  3. Everything the cell absorbs - dust-absorbed stellar FUV/optical included,
     since gas and dust share `recPDF` (photon_mod:1920-1924) - comes back out
     at 24.38 eV, where the cell is ~700 per cell opaque. It is absorbed on the
     spot, by H2 and H0, and re-emitted from the same PDF: the packets cycle
     (the tripled step count of D-224) and the path-length estimator fills the
     cell with field (D-225: all of it diffuse, none stellar).
  4. That field photoionizes H0; the thermal balance sees the heating (D-221,
     D-222) and the cell flips hot.
  5. Hot, the factor is negligible, the band empties, the cell cools - and the
     cycle repeats. The collapses at iterations 6 and 10 follow the coldest
     iterations (median end Te 102 K at 5, 133 K at 9; D-224).

It explains every regularity measured since D-217: heating from 15.4-24.6 eV
only (D-221, D-222) - the bin is the band's top bin; a field in cells no stellar
photon reaches (D-224, D-225); no hot neighbour needed (D-223); flipping cells
that lose their field the iteration after (D-218); and the collapse surviving
every fix to the chemistry, seed, cooling and hydrogen budget (D-209 to D-220),
none of which touched the emission spectrum. The 19.8 eV He I 2^3S term is real
and dominates the band when the gas is warm (iteration 4, hot cells throughout),
but at P ~ 1e-4-1e-3 it cannot fill a cell.

**Proposed fix (not applied; awaiting approval).** Start the analytic He I and
He II branches in `fb_ff` at their threshold bins, `HeIPnuP` and `HeIIPnuP`, as
the H I branch already starts at `HIPnuP`. Bins between a table's top edge and
the threshold then take the table's own top value, which is zero at both edges
(the tables list 0 at 1.7999 and 3.9996 Ryd). No constant, no gate.

**Where the fix touches MOCASSIN outside the PDR.** Every model's He I continuum
in those two bins, and He II's in one. In an H II region at ~1e4 K the spurious
factor is exp(0.0158 x 157890/1e4) ~ 1.3 times a cross-section 4.5e-5 of the
threshold value - negligible, so benchmark changes should be at the noise level.
That is expected, not yet checked.

### A second analysis, from another checkout (2026-09-11)

The user brought an analysis made in a separate testing checkout. Its measured
facts agree with D-224/D-225: no stellar penetration of the PDR, re-emission
trapped in the emitting cell, `recursionLimit = 5000`. It identified the
channel correctly - dust absorptions become "diffuse" packets and sample a
`recPDF` that pools gas and dust emission - and attributed the leak to the He I
2^3S term at 19.8 eV and its `MAX(5000., Te)` clamp. It proposed two tiers.

**Assessment.**
  - The 19.8 eV attribution is contradicted by D-226 at the iterations that
    matter: from iteration 5 on, 99.9-100% of the band's re-emission and field
    in cold cells is at 24.38 eV. The clamp also works the other way from the
    claim: alpha scales as T^-0.678, so the 5000 K floor makes the cold-gas rate
    smaller, not larger.
  - **Tier 1** (separate dust and gas re-emission; `dustEmi` with gas present):
    pooling the cell's total emissivity is MOCASSIN's standard re-emission and
    is exact at equilibrium. It is the channel by which dust-absorbed energy
    reaches the bad bin, not the defect. Splitting it would change every dusty
    model and leave bin 465 in `recPDF` for gas absorptions. A possible design
    change on its own merits, to be benchmarked separately; not needed for this.
  - **Tier 2** (zero ionizing continuum and the 2^3S/He II Lyman terms where
    A_V > 1 or Te < 1000 K): a zone gate with hardcoded thresholds, which
    CLAUDE.md rules out, and it would suppress the symptom while leaving the
    defect in every other cell and model.
  - Not in that analysis: the start-bin defect in `fb_ff`.

**Open, separate from the fix.** x(He+) of 1e-4-2e-2 in shielded cold cells
(iteration 4: 2.2e-2 in the cells about to flip, above their x(H+)) with no
field above 24.6 eV reaching them. Probably He ionized by the trapped field in
the cascade or carried from the hot phase; to be checked after the fix, when the
cascade is gone.

## D-227 - the fix, and its test (2026-09-11)

**Decision.** Approved by the user after D-226: apply the start-bin fix and rerun.

**Change** (`emission_mod.f90`, `fb_ff`). The analytic He I branch ran for
`i >= HeINuEdgeP(nlimGammaHeI)`; He II's for `i >= HeIINuEdgeP(nlimGammaHeII)`.
Each now splits at its threshold: at and above `HeIPnuP` (`HeIIPnuP`) the
ground-state continuum exactly as before; between the table's top edge and the
threshold, free-free only (`ffCoeff1`, `ffCoeff2`). That is the physics of those
bins - no ground-state recombination below the threshold - and it matches the
tables, which go to zero at their top edges (1.7999 and 3.9996 Ryd). No constant
and no condition on the cell. If a grid ever puts the table edge above the
threshold, the branch starts at the edge as before and nothing changes.

**Checked, and not changed.** `update_mod` reads the same cross-section blocks
with the same index pattern (`xSecArray(j-IPnuP+1+HeISingXSecP(1)-1)`, lines 226
and 1886) but both loops run `do j = IPnuP, highNuP`, from each ion's own
threshold, so the index never leaves the He I or He II block there.

**Predictions** (stated before the run):
  - In cold cells, P(re-emitted packet born in 15.4-24.6 eV) drops from 0.35-0.98
    at iteration 6 to the level of iteration 4 (~1e-4-1e-3), carried by 19.8 eV.
  - The collapse at iteration 6 does not occur: no iteration moves thousands of
    PDR cells cold -> hot, and the median f_mol no longer swings to 0.24.
  - The step count does not triple at iteration 6.
  - If the oscillation persists at smaller amplitude, what remains is a second
    mechanism, and the census will say what carries the heating.
  - Outside the PDR the change is ~1e-5 of He I's threshold emission at 1e4 K;
    a standard H II benchmark should confirm that separately.

**Run.** `runs/d227-hei-fix`, fixture `hiipdr-split`, 12 iterations, with the
D-224..D-226 diagnostics in place. Compared against `runs/d224-trace` (the same
fixture without the fix).

**What is NOT known.** Everything the run is for.


### Result (2026-09-11)

`runs/d227-hei-fix`, fixture `hiipdr-split`, 12 iterations, 14 ranks, clean
build of all four flavours. Compared with `runs/d224-trace`: same fixture,

### What is open after the fix

  1. **The converged count is ~0% at every iteration** (0.007-0.026%) although
     the model has stopped moving. Cause, read from the code: `pdrFcritConv`
     defaults to 1 and no fixture sets it, so `pdrStep` clears `lgConverged` in
     any PDR cell whose 3D-PDR heat and cool differ by more than `pdrFcrit`
     (0.5%) at MOCASSIN's Te (pdr_mod:3107-3115). D-176 and D-193 concluded that
     balance is not required under the contract; D-181's converging run set
     `pdrFcritConv 0`, and the default was never changed. A decision for the
     user: the default, and the fixture length (D-181 needed 18-22 iterations).
  2. **"Ion balance not reached" in ~50% of cells** - `ionBalance` hitting
     `maxIterateX` before x(H0), x(He0) and x(He+) change by less than 1%
     between its internal steps. It sets `lgBlack`, not `lgConverged`. Probably
     the relative change of small He+ fractions in cold cells; not measured.
  3. **x(He+) rises steadily in the cold cells**: 5.6e-4, 6.3e-4, 7.1e-4,
     8.1e-4, 9.8e-4, 1.19e-3 over iterations 7-12, while x(H+) falls 5.5e-4 ->
     2.8e-4. Nothing ionizes helium in shielded cold gas at that rate. Candidate
     links: item 2, and the D-220 rescaling. Unexplained; if it keeps growing it
     feeds the real 19.8 eV term.
  4. **Median Te 13 K** against the reference's 24-36 K at a weaker field (above).
  5. Mean f_mol drifts down slowly (0.847 at 8 -> 0.824 at 12) with the < 0.01
     bin growing 3.4% -> 5.2% while the median is flat: a small population
     losing its molecules. Possibly item 3.
  6. The effect of the fix outside the PDR (expected ~1e-5 of He I's threshold
     emission at 1e4 K) has not been checked on a standard H II benchmark.

## D-228 - the convergence default, and fixture length (2026-09-11)

**Decision.** Approved by the user after D-227.

**Why.** D-227's model stopped moving - median f_mol flat at 0.9455 from
iteration 9, median |df_mol| 6e-4, 1.2% of cells moving more than 0.1% - and
MOCASSIN reported 0.007% converged. The per-cell test (D-155, D-179: x(H0)
and x(H2) against their iteration-start values, `convLimit 0.10`) is not what
held it there. `pdrStep` clears `lgConverged` in any cell whose 3D-PDR heat and
cool differ by more than `pdrFcrit` = 0.5% at MOCASSIN's Te (D-032,
pdr_mod:3107-3115), and it runs after `updateCell`, so it has the last word.

D-176 found that test meaningless once MOCASSIN owns the temperature; D-193
annotated it "left switchable purely as a probe"; D-181's run that converged
(86.4% at 22 iterations, every species' total content within ~1%) set
`pdrFcritConv 0` in its input. The default stayed 1 and no fixture set it, so
every run since has been judged by it. D-198 made the contract unconditional,
which leaves no configuration in which the test measures anything solved.

**Change.**
  - `common_mod`: `pdrFcritConv = 0`. The switch stays, as a probe.
  - `maxIterateMC 22` in all nine PDR fixtures: hiipdr, hiipdr-contract,
    hiipdr-couple1, hiipdr-d190, hiipdr-d190-noavail, hiipdr-split, ifront
    (were 12), v1slab and v2slab (were 8). D-181 needed 18-22 iterations; the
    slabs have not been re-measured at that length.

**Not changed.** The per-cell criterion itself, `convLimit 0.10`, and the
"ion balance not reached" count (a separate `lgBlack` flag).

**Predictions.** The converged fraction rises as the model settles rather than
sitting at ~0%. D-227's movement fell to 1.2% of cells by iteration 12, so
most PDR cells should pass once the clearing is gone; how high it goes is set by
the per-cell x(H0) test, where x(H0) is a ~5% residual in molecular gas and its
relative change is amplified (D-198's note). If it plateaus well below ~90%,
the next question is which of the two per-cell tests fails, and where.

**Run.** `runs/d228-converge`, fixture `hiipdr-split` at 22 iterations, with the
D-227 fix and all diagnostics.

**What is NOT known.** Everything the run is for.


### Result (2026-09-11)

`runs/d228-converge`, fixture `hiipdr-split`, `maxIterateMC 22 95.`, the D-227
fix, `pdrFcritConv` 0 by default. Clean exit after **5 iterations**, 7:46 per
processor.

     it   converged, D-228   converged, D-227 (clearing on)
      1         0.00%              0.00%
      2         0.0066             0.0066
      3        72.2               72.3
      4        26.0                0.0066
      5        95.86               0.026     -> D-228 stops: 95.86 >= minConvergence 95

The stop is `iteration_mod:3072`: `totPercent >= minConvergence` once the PDR
has had a pass (D-062). `pdrFcritConv` changes only the converged flag, not
the physics, so D-227 shows what D-228 stopped short of:

     from iteration 5 to 12 (D-227)
     median Te, PDR           90 K   ->  13 K
     median f_mol            0.916   ->  0.9455 (flat from 9)
     cells moving > 0.1%       37%   ->  1.2%

**What it means.** The prediction recorded above was met and then some: without
the clearing, the per-cell test passes almost everywhere as soon as the
molecules stop moving by 10% per iteration. But that test is
|dx(H0)/x| <= `convLimit` and |dx(H2)/x| <= `convLimit` (D-155, D-179) - it does
not test the temperature. In an H II region Te follows the ionization, so
MOCASSIN never needed to. In a PDR the molecular coolants set Te independently,
and here it falls sevenfold after the run has declared itself converged. The
project rule - "a convergence percentage is only as good as the quantity it
measures" - again: the 95.86% is real for x(H0) and x(H2) and says nothing about
Te.

D-181's 22-iteration run never met this because it never reached 95%: the
oscillation kept the per-cell test near 86%.

**Options, for the user:**
  1. Test Te per cell alongside x(H0) and x(H2), at the same `convLimit`,
     against its iteration-start value (`TeIterStart` already exists). Physics:
     the thermal state is one of the quantities being converged. D-227's numbers
     say it would hold the run until ~iteration 9-10, where Te moves < 2%.
  2. Leave the test and set the fixtures' `minConvergence` above 100 so every run
     goes the full 22. Simple, but it hides the gap rather than closing it, and a
     user's own input would still stop early.
  3. Both.

Recommended: 1. Not applied pending a decision.

**Not yet committed.** The D-228 change stands (the clearing had no meaning
under the contract) but is incomplete without a temperature criterion.

## D-229 - the temperature belongs in the convergence test (2026-09-11)

**Decision.** Chosen by the user after D-228, over two alternatives: setting the
fixtures' `minConvergence` above 100 so runs never stop early, or both.

**Why.** MOCASSIN's per-cell test is |dx(H0)/x| and (D-179) |dx(H2)/x| against
the iteration-start values, at `convLimit`. It has never tested Te. In an H II
region that is defensible: the temperature follows the ionization, so a settled
x(H0) implies a settled Te. In a PDR it does not - the molecular coolants set
the temperature, and the two can settle at different rates. D-228 measured the
consequence: 95.86% converged at iteration 5, the run stopped by
`minConvergence`, and the same physics (D-227) went on to take the median PDR Te
from 90 K to 13 K and the median f_mol from 0.916 to 0.9455 over the next four
iterations.

**Change** (`update_mod`, the `lgConverged` block). A third condition:

    lgCvTe = |TeUsed - TeIterStart(cellP)| / TeIterStart(cellP) <= XHILimit

guarded on `TeIterStart` being allocated (it is, in every flavour -
grid_mod:1671, no #ifdef) and positive, so a cell with no previous value is not
failed for lacking one. `lgConverged` is now the AND of all three.
`cvFailTe` counts temperature-only failures beside `cvFailH0`, `cvFailH2` and
`cvFailBoth`, under `teProbe` as they are.

**Predictions.** The run no longer stops at iteration 5. D-227's Te series -
310, 90, 34, 19, 15, 14, 13, 13, 13 K - moves by more than 10% until about
iteration 9 and by ~1-2% after it, so convergence should be reached around
iterations 9-12 rather than 5, and the state at that point should match D-227's
iteration 12 (median f_mol 0.9455, median Te 13 K). If it instead runs all 22
iterations, some population is still moving in Te and the census says which.

**Run.** `runs/d229-teconv`, `hiipdr-split` at 22 iterations.

**What is NOT known.** Everything the run is for. In particular whether a 10%
per-cell tolerance on Te is the right one; `convLimit` sets all three.


### Result (2026-09-11)

`runs/d229-teconv`, fixture `hiipdr-split`, 22 iterations, 36:03 per processor,
clean exit. The prediction was met: the run does not stop at iteration 5, and it
converges around 9-12 rather than there.

     it    converged   median f_mol   median Te   median |df_mol|   cells moving > 0.1%
      4     0.013%       0.8297         309 K        0.253            62.8%
      5     0.21         0.9180          90          0.055            36.5
      6     0.80         0.9379          33.7        0.015             5.9
      7     1.14         0.9435          19.3        0.0039            6.0
      8     5.01         0.9450          15.0        0.0017            7.6
      9    50.7          0.9454          13.7        0.0008            5.3
     10    78.7          0.9454          13.4        0.0007            2.0
     12    83.2          0.9454          13.2        0.0006            1.1
     16    85.4          0.9454          13.1        0.0006            5.1
     22    85.9          0.9455          13.0        0.0005            3.6

Against D-228 (same physics, no Te test): 26.0% at iteration 4 and 95.86% at 5.
The temperature criterion holds the run through the cooling - median Te 309 ->
90 -> 34 -> 19 -> 15 -> 13.7 K over iterations 4-9 - and lets it pass when that
stops, which is what it was added to do.

**The state is D-227's**, as it must be (the criterion changes when the run
stops, not what it computes): median f_mol 0.9455 against 0.9455, median Te
13.0 K against 13.2 K. The axis profile is *smoother* after ten more
iterations: PDR-zone Te 14.0-21.9 K (median 18.0) against D-227's 14.1-50.6 K
(median 18.0) at iteration 12, and the scatter in x(H2) between neighbouring
cells is gone - D-227 still carried a 50.6 K cell at the PDR edge and single
cells at 24.7 and 15.4 K where D-229 has 17.6, 18.0 and 18.0 K.

**The plateau, and what is still open.** The converged fraction stops at 85-86%
from iteration 14 and does not rise. Over the same iterations the share of cells
moving more than 0.1% per iteration comes back up from 1.06% (iteration 12) to
3.6-5%, and |df_mol| p90 from 0.0149 to ~0.022. So the residual is a churning
population, not a monotone approach - the same ~14% D-181 saw and called cells
crossing branches. What it is has not been measured here:
  - which of the three tests those cells fail (`cvFailH0`, `cvFailH2`,
    `cvFailTe` exist but print only under `teProbe`, which is 0);
  - where they sit - the census bins by outcome group, not by convergence;
  - whether a 10% per-cell tolerance on Te is right at all: `convLimit` sets the
    same number for x(H0), x(H2) and Te, and Monte Carlo noise on a cell's
    temperature is not measured either.

**Also still open** (D-227, unchanged by this): the PDR gas is 2-10x colder than
standalone 3D-PDR at a stronger field; x(He+) climbs in shielded cold cells;
about half the cells report "ion balance not reached"; the H II benchmark has
not been re-run since the He I fix.

**The per-species content report of D-178** (`cvSpNow`/`cvSpName`, Cloudy's
iteration-level check on total content) does exist and prints as `! CVSPEC`
lines - iteration_mod:2449 - but behind `teProbe /= 0`, and no fixture sets
`teProbe`, so this run's log carries none. The same gate hides `cvFailH0`,
`cvFailH2` and `cvFailTe`. So one run with `teProbe` set would answer both open
questions above at once: which test the churning ~14% fail, and whether the
total content per species is stable to ~1% as D-181 reported.

"no longer printed anywhere in the source". It is printed; I wrote that from a
grep whose output was truncated, without reading the block.)
